extracted.intended_audience: readers interested in 18th-century secret societies, political historians, general readers
extracted.subtask_description: A historical account describing the organization, recruitment, instruction, secrecy, and political aims of the Order of the Illuminati (letters, rituals, and operational methods). Focus is on how members are selected, prepared, advanced, and placed into positions of influence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Selection of pupils
rubrics_metrics.description: Pupils are 'a set of picked subjects, whose characters and peculiar biases were well known by their conduct during their noviciate as Minervals.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Choose those unlikely to 'boggle at very free sentiments' — younger sons and men of talent without fortune; prefer recruits predisposed to doctrines removing restraints on youthful passions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exclude religionists from higher mysteries
rubrics_metrics.description: Explicit rule: 'No religionist must, on any account, be admitted into these' (higher mysteries).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Higher degrees are reserved for those who have 'laid aside his prejudices' and are amenable to the Order's work of 'discovery and extirpation of superstition and prejudices.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Portray Superiors as men of superior minds
rubrics_metrics.description: Pupils are taught that their Superiors 'were men of distinguished talents, and were Superiors for this reason alone.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Maintain the idea that Superiors have enlarged views beyond nations, deserving reverence; pupils typically know only their Mentor to reinforce this impression.

rubrics_metrics.name: Secrecy in organization and operations
rubrics_metrics.description: Directive: 'All mention of degrees, or other business of the Order, must be carefully avoided, even in the meetings with other members: "For the Order wishes to be secret, and to work in silence".'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Secrecy protects the Order from ruling powers and 'gives a greater zest to the whole'; avoid open discussion of internal structure or degrees.

rubrics_metrics.name: Instruction methods: controlled readings and returned writings
rubrics_metrics.description: Instruction is given partly by verbal instruction of the Mentor, partly by writings which 'must be punctually returned, and partly read by the pupil at the Mentor's house (but without taking extracts).'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Pupils produce rescripts containing discussions, anecdotes, and character descriptions; these exercises are the chief means of advancement and must be zealously continued.

rubrics_metrics.name: Gradual doctrinal preparation (curriculum progression)
rubrics_metrics.description: Initial readings are confined 'at first to moralists and reasoning historians' to prepare pupils for 'works of a bolder flight' (e.g., Robinet, Helvetius).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Introduce controversial or radical works only after pupils are prepared; if an intrant already possesses strong books, neither praise nor condemn them publicly until readiness is assessed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of surveillance and mutual espionage among members
rubrics_metrics.description: Operational rule: 'every person shall be made a spy on another and on all around him.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Surveillance is intended to discover trust-worthiness and to build a council of reliable members who will plan means to 'drive by degrees the enemies of reason and of humanity out of the world.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Promotion and advancement based on ideological conformity
rubrics_metrics.description: 'Rulers who are members must be promoted through the ranks of the Order only in proportion as they acknowledge the goodness of its great object.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Members who appear more disposed to external authorities (e.g., Princes) than to the Order are deemed unfit to rise; advancement is tied to active support of the Order's aims.

rubrics_metrics.name: Political infiltration and placement in institutions
rubrics_metrics.description: The Order aimed to 'procure the advancement of Illuminati into all important civil offices' and used influence to place members as tutors, in courts of justice, and in university chairs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Deliberately place members in positions (ecclesiastical dignities, academic chairs, tutorships, public offices) to extend influence and implement the Order's objectives.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of front organizations/reading societies
rubrics_metrics.description: After setbacks the Order reconstituted 'under the name of the GERMAN UNION, appearing in the form of READING SOCIETIES.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Operate publicly under benign or scholarly guises to continue covert objectives even if internal papers are exposed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Employ rhetorical/ritual adaptation to conceal aims (Masonic Christianity)
rubrics_metrics.description: Philo's plan: present the Order's doctrines as 'the secrets of genuine Free Masonry' and a form of 'Masonic Christianity' so that fanatics are not alarmed while 'secret doctrines' are inculcated.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use familiar religious symbols, rituals, and reinterpretations to cloak radical principles; rituals and Disciplina Arcani-style secrecy make doctrines acceptable to influential recruits (even Popes and Kings after trials).

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of female auxiliaries for intelligence and finance
rubrics_metrics.description: Project for a Sisterhood: 'It will be of great service, and procure us both much information and money... It should consist of two classes, the virtuous and the freer hearted...under the direction of men.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Organize covert female networks to gather information and funds while keeping their subordination to male direction secret from members.

rubrics_metrics.name: Practical opportunism in acquiring materials and means
rubrics_metrics.description: Spartacus: 'To collect unpublished works, and information from the archives of States, will be a most useful service... It will do more good in our hands than by remaining for 1000 years on the dusty shelf.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rationalize appropriation of documents and materials if perceived political advantage outweighs conventional proprieties; intelligence-gathering is integral to strategy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Maintain plausible deniability via 'pious frauds' and explanation later
rubrics_metrics.description: Plan: 'We must, 1st, gradually explain away all our preparatory pious frauds. And when persons of discernment find fault, we must desire them to consider the end of all our labour.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use staged deceptions or tolerated pious appearances to prepare audiences; justify controversial preparatory acts by appeal to the ultimate aims when challenged.
